programmes.funder: Anzisha Prize (African Leadership Academy and Mastercard Foundation)
programmes.amount_note: Historic prize pool of up to US$100,000 shared among fellows, plus a multi-year fellowship
programmes.deadline_note: Applications historically opened in the first quarter with fellows announced later in the year
programmes.reopen_note: The programme has evolved from a prize into a longer venture-building fellowship. Verify the current model on anzishaprize.org.

eligibility.other_note: African entrepreneurs aged 15-22 running a revenue-generating business

programmes.funder: Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa (IDC)
programmes.amount_note: Concessionary funding from ZAR 1 million upwards (typically to ZAR 50 million) at reduced interest rates for youth-owned businesses, with a portion sometimes structured as a grant or interest subsidy.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit an online funding application to the IDC.
Basic assessment and allocation to a sector team.
Due diligence.
Credit committee approval and legal agreements.

eligibility.other_note: Requires majority ownership by South African youth (18-35). Minimum deal size makes it unsuitable for very small startups.

programmes.amount_note: Debt, quasi-equity and equity funding from ZAR 250,000 to ZAR 15 million for black-owned start-ups and early-stage businesses, including a franchise sub-product.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling applications through the NEF online system.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the NEF applications portal.
Submit the business plan and financial model.
Screening, due diligence and site visit.
Investment committee approval and legal agreements.

eligibility.other_note: Requires black ownership of at least 50.1% (with black management control) and the entrepreneur to be involved in day-to-day operations.

programmes.funder: Department of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI) / SARS
programmes.amount_note: 150% deduction of qualifying R&D operating expenditure against taxable income, plus accelerated depreciation on R&D capital assets. There is no cash payment; the benefit depends on the company's tax position.
programmes.deadline_note: Pre-approval is required: expenditure only qualifies from the date DSTI receives the application. The incentive was extended by legislation beyond its previous 2022 sunset date.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit the pre-approval application to DSTI before starting the R&D (or before the expenditure you want to claim).
DSTI adjudication committee approves the activities.
Claim the 150% deduction in the corporate income tax return.
Submit annual progress reports to DSTI.

documents_required.doc: DSTI R&D tax incentive application form
Technical description of the R&D activities

eligibility.other_note: South African taxpayers conducting scientific or technological R&D in South Africa. Excludes routine testing, market research, social science research and internal business process software in most cases.

programmes.name_local: SA SME Fund - venture and fund investments
programmes.name_en: SA SME Fund - venture and fund investments
programmes.amount_note: A private-sector-funded vehicle (capitalised by JSE-listed corporates) that invests into venture capital and SME funds, and through its Venture Capital Fund of Funds into South African startups indirectly. It rarely invests directly into companies.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; startups should approach the underlying VC funds backed by the SA SME Fund rather than the fund itself.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify SA SME Fund portfolio VC managers.
Approach the relevant manager with your round.
Standard VC diligence and investment.

eligibility.other_note: South African businesses; the fund's mandate includes a strong focus on black-owned and township enterprises through specific vehicles.

programmes.name_local: Seda Technology Programme (Stp) incubation and technology transfer support
programmes.name_en: Seda Technology Programme (Stp) incubation and technology transfer support
programmes.funder: Small Enterprise Development Agency (Seda), now part of the Small Enterprise Development Finance Agency (SEDFA)
programmes.amount_note: Support for technology transfer, quality and standards certification and incubation. Historically the technology transfer grant covered up to about ZAR 600,000 (with a co-contribution) towards machinery and equipment for small enterprises; quality certification support was smaller.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are made through Seda/SEDFA branch offices. Seda was merged with sefa and the Cooperative Banks Development Agency into SEDFA in 2024-2025, and product names and ceilings are being revised.
programmes.reopen_note: Seda's functions moved into the Small Enterprise Development Finance Agency (SEDFA) following the 2024 merger. Product terms are being re-published under the SEDFA brand; check with a provincial SEDFA office for current ceilings and open windows.

procedure_steps.detail: Visit a Seda/SEDFA branch or incubation centre.
Business diagnostic and referral to the relevant product.
Submit the application with quotations.
Approval and payment to the supplier.

eligibility.other_note: South African micro and small enterprises, with priority for black-owned, women-owned, youth-owned and rural enterprises.

programmes.funder: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic), administered with the IDC
programmes.amount_note: Two schemes. Product Process Development (PPD) Scheme: maximum grant R2 million, covering 50%-85% of qualifying costs depending on BEE ownership, for small, very small and micro enterprises. Matching Scheme: maximum grant R5 million, covering 50%-75% of qualifying costs based on BEE ownership, available to all enterprises and individuals.
programmes.deadline_note: No closing date is published; applications are submitted to spiiapplications@thedtic.gov.za and assessed as received.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the development represents a significant advance in technology and that development and subsequent production will take place within South Africa.
Choose the scheme (PPD for small/very small/micro enterprises, Matching Scheme for all enterprises).
Submit the application to spiiapplications@thedtic.gov.za (contact Ramoroa Molose, +27 12 394 5655).
Assessment; if approved, claim qualifying costs (personnel, materials, capital items, software, testing, patents, subcontracting, QA) against milestones.

documents_required.doc: Technical project description showing significant technology advance

documents_required.note: Excludes production, marketing and basic research

documents_required.doc: Proof that IP will reside in a South African registered company

eligibility.other_note: 'Development should represent significant advance in technology'; 'Development and subsequent production must take place within South Africa'; 'Intellectual Property to reside in South African registered company'. Grant percentage rises with B-BBEE ownership levels.

programmes.source_snippet: The SPII is designed to promote technology development in South Africa's industry, through the provision of financial assistance ... Product Process Development (PPD) Scheme ... maximum grant R2 million ... Matching Scheme ... maximum grant R5 million.

programmes.name_local: Support Programme for Industrial Innovation (SPII) - Matching Scheme
programmes.name_en: Support Programme for Industrial Innovation (SPII) - Matching Scheme
programmes.funder: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic), administered by the IDC
programmes.amount_note: Non-repayable grant of up to ZAR 5 million per project. The grant covers 50% of qualifying costs for applicants with 0-25% BEE ownership, 65% for 25.1-50% BEE ownership or >50% women/persons-with-disabilities ownership, and 75% for >50% BEE ownership.
programmes.deadline_note: Open call with no fixed deadline; applications are assessed by an adjudication committee that meets periodically.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the project is pre-competitive product or process development, not routine engineering.
Complete the SPII application form with a detailed technical and cost breakdown.
Submit to the dtic SPII office (enquiries +27 12 394 1576).
Technical evaluation and adjudication committee decision; grant paid against verified milestone claims.

eligibility.other_note: South African registered enterprises and individuals. Grant share depends on B-BBEE ownership level. IP must be registered in South Africa and the resulting production must occur mainly in South Africa.

programmes.source_snippet: Provides financial assistance to all enterprises and individuals in the form of a non-repayable grant. A percentage of 'qualifying' costs incurred in the development activities of a specified development project. R 5 million (maximum grant)

programmes.funder: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
programmes.amount_note: Non-repayable grant of up to ZAR 2 million for small, very small and micro enterprises and individuals. Covers 50% of qualifying pre-competitive development costs for 0-25% BEE ownership, 75% for 25.1-50% BEE ownership or >50% women/persons-with-disabilities ownership, and 85% for >50% BEE ownership.
programmes.deadline_note: Open call with no fixed deadline.

procedure_steps.detail: Prepare the technical project description and cost breakdown.
Submit the PPD application to the dtic SPII office.
Technical and financial evaluation.
Adjudication and milestone-based disbursement.

eligibility.other_note: Restricted to small, very small and micro enterprises and to individuals; higher grant percentages than the Matching Scheme.

programmes.source_snippet: Provides financial assistance to small, very small and micro-enterprises and individuals in the form of a non-repayable grant... R2 million (maximum grant)

programmes.name_local: Technology and Human Resources for Industry Programme (THRIP)
programmes.name_en: Technology and Human Resources for Industry Programme (THRIP)
programmes.funder: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic), administered by the NRF
programmes.amount_note: Cost-sharing grant for collaborative industry-academia R&D, historically matching industry contributions on a 1:1 basis up to about ZAR 8 million per project per year, with more favourable ratios for SMEs and black-owned firms.
programmes.deadline_note: THRIP operates through annual calls administered by the National Research Foundation; the call window and terms are published each year.
programmes.reopen_note: THRIP is administered on the dtic's behalf by the NRF and has historically issued one call per financial year (South African fiscal year runs April-March). Confirm the current call on the dtic incentives page and the NRF website.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify a South African university or science council partner.
Prepare the joint R&D and student training plan.
Submit through the NRF online system by the call deadline.
Peer review and award; industry contribution matched.

eligibility.other_note: Requires a South African higher education or science council partner and postgraduate student training as part of the project.

programmes.name_en: Technology Innovation Agency (TIA) Seed Fund Programme
programmes.amount_note: No seed-fund ceiling is published on the TIA funding instruments page. Related instruments do publish caps: the Grassroots Innovation Programme has a maximum R200,000 technology development grant and the Technology Acquisition and Deployment Fund a maximum of R1 million over 24 months. Do not assume a Seed Fund maximum.
programmes.deadline_note: TIA funds through periodic calls, often via implementing partners (universities, science councils, incubators). Check the TIA site for the current call; contact customerservice@tia.org.za.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify the correct instrument for your technology readiness level (Seed Fund TRL 3-8; Technology Development Fund TRL 4-7; Commercialisation Support Fund TRL 8-9).
Apply through the open call or through a TIA implementing partner.
Technical and commercial due diligence, then contracting and milestone-based disbursement.

documents_required.doc: Application form for the relevant TIA instrument
Technology/prototype development plan with TRL evidence

documents_required.note: Standard for South African public funding

eligibility.other_note: Seed Fund is designed to 'assist innovators at Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), Science Councils (SCs) and Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs)' to convert research outputs into prototypes and commercialisable ideas, at TRL 3-8.

programmes.source_snippet: SEED Fund ... assist innovators at Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), Science Councils (SCs) and Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) ... TRL 3-8.

programmes.amount_note: Larger funding instrument supporting technology development from proof of concept through to pre-commercial demonstration; historically funding several million rand per project depending on stage.
programmes.deadline_note: TIA opens instrument-specific calls; there is no permanent open window for all instruments.
programmes.reopen_note: TIA publishes open calls on tia.org.za/funding-instruments. Between calls, applicants can register their project for notification.

procedure_steps.detail: Check the TIA funding instruments page for an open call.
Submit a concept note.
Full application if invited.
Due diligence and funding agreement with milestone tranches.

eligibility.other_note: South African registered entities, including SMEs, higher education institutions and science councils.
